angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,189,647 km at 162.57 pc = 0.1 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.1513 +/- 0.0194 mas (same row, RUWE 1.09): 162.57 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.71 +/- 0.05 solar radii from Clark et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-778 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..207C/abstract): 1,189,647 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.4 +/- 0.05 solar masses from Clark et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-778 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..207C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6643 +/- 150 K from Clark et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-778 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..207C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Clark et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-778 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..207C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-778.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.118, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
